scope: Theorem 5.1 (Equality soundness for degree-two shortcode) of the manuscript “The Unique Games Theorem” (preprints/The-Unique-Games-Theorem-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 102 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 04d0290a9cb7ee81), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 22-23. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every η ∈ (0, 1) there are α ∈ (0, 1], an integer rs ≥ 1, and an integer ℓ0, depending only on η, with the following property. For every ℓ ≥ ℓ0 there is m0 = m0(η, ℓ) such that, for every m ≥ m0 and every function f : Matℓ,m → Fℓ 2, if Pr M,a,l  f(M) = f(M + al⊤ )  ≥ η, (5.2) then some slice S as in Equation (5.1), with nr, nc ≤ rs, and some z ∈ Fm 2 , u ∈ Fℓ 2 satisfy Pr M|S [f(M) = Mz + u] ≥ α. (5.3) 22 Here M, a ∈ Fℓ 2, and l ∈ Fm 2 are independent and uniform, and M | S is uniform on the slice. No folding condition is imposed on f.
